traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Loranthaceae with Eremolepidaceae, which APG and WCVP join to it (their extra states read as sometimes): leaves usually opposite, sometimes alternate; leaves simple; margins entire; veins single, pinnate or parallel; leaves evergreen; stipules absent; plants usually hermaphrodite, sometimes dioecious, rarely monoecious; ovary usually inferior, sometimes half inferior; floral cup absent; joined corolla tubular; stems woody; flowers in cymes, in racemes, in spikes or in umbels, sometimes in catkins; flowers actinomorphic or zygomorphic; irregular flowers bilabiate; perianth usually sepals and petals, often tepals, sometimes absent; fruit berry or drupe, rarely nut; stamens (3-) 5 to 6 (-9); carpels 3 to 4. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.flower_merosity.note: DELTA Loranthaceae (read 2026-10-16): corolla and stamens mostly 5-6, up to 9 (low 4 from wider knowledge).

traits.flower_symmetry.note: DELTA, Loranthaceae (read 2026-10-16): flowers regular to somewhat irregular, any irregularity being in the perianth (a tube often bent and split down one side); radial leads, with zygomorphic flowers as a minority.

traits.fruit_type.note: POWO Loranthaceae general information (read 2026-10-17; about 77 genera and 950 spp per the Flora Zambesiaca account): the Kew handbook account gives a one-seeded berry throughout, with the dry winged nut only in Nuytsia; the Cayman account calls the fruit berry-like and the West African account berry or drupe. Berry leads across the family.

traits.inflorescence.note: POWO Loranthaceae (read 2026-10-17): flowers mostly in three-flowered dichasia (small cymes), these set on axillary or terminal racemes, panicles, umbels or heads, solitary flowers rare; the Flora Zambesiaca account repeats the frequent triads. The cymose unit is what is usual; spikes are not named, so they drop to sometimes and catkin to rarely.
